I am having some troubles in obtaining the metric/weak invariance for my model. 
Here the model
CFA_model2 <- '
 IC =~ Q19_1 + Q19_2 + Q19_3
 PC =~ Q19_4 + Q19_5 + Q19_6
 ATT =~ ATT_1 + ATT_2
 SN =~ SN_1 + SN_2
 PBC =~ PBC1_1 + PBC2_1  
 INT =~ INT_1 + INT_2 + INT_3'

I run the following functions:
#configural invariance
fit1 <- cfa(CFA_model2, data = df_cleaned1,  meanstructure=T, estimator="WLSMV", group = "residence")

# weak invariance
fit2 <- cfa(CFA_model2, data = df_cleaned1,  meanstructure=T, estimator="WLSMV", group = "residence", std.lv=TRUE,   group.equal = "loadings")   

Then:
lavTestLRT(fit1, fit2)
Results:
Df AIC BIC Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq) fit1 150 210.74  
fit2 159 290.84 84.096 9 2.472e-14 ***

So what I did was running other tests:
lavInspect(fit2, "sampstat")
lavTech(fit2, "sampstat")
lavTestScore(fit2)

Hi Giulia,

here are a few remarks from my point of view - others may strongly disagree:

1. You are using WLSMV estimation for the CFA. For the SEM you rely on ML. If your data is continuous or you have enough categories (see https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2Fa0029315), then I would estimate both models with ML.
2. Since the data are probably not normally distributed, I would think about a "robust" estimator (MLM or MLR). It's still a ML estimation, but with correction for se and chi-squared. Consequently, you can do the invariance test with a "robust" variant ("satorra.bentler.2010").
3. Metric (partial) invariance is sufficient, since you only compare regression coefficients and not mean differences (correct?).
4. In your SEM I can't see that the constraints for the measurement model are incorporated.
5. The Wald tests are not wrong. However, I don't understand the meaning perfectly. The approach is at least exploratory. Normally you have hypotheses in advance, don't you? Detached from that, you can do it without the Wald tests and test the moderators with your SEM. For example for ATT->IC you can include the following syntax: mod.ATT.IC := a1 - a.
6 I don't understand the line under ## Fixed Covriances. The covariance between ATT and IC is not fixed, but freely estimated. At the same time ATT is explained by IC. Possibly I am reading the syntax wrong at this point - sorry then.
7. I personally would not appply the bootstrap and use Monte Carlo CI. That is just as effective and more efficient.

HTH

Christian

Hi Giulia,

here are a few remarks from my point of view - others may strongly disagree:

1. You are using WLSMV estimation for the CFA. For the SEM you rely on ML. If your data is continuous or you have enough categories (see https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2Fa0029315), then I would estimate both models with ML.
2. Since the data are probably not normally distributed, I would think about a "robust" estimator (MLM or MLR). It's still a ML estimation, but with correction for se and chi-squared. Consequently, you can do the invariance test with a "robust" variant ("satorra.bentler.2010").
3. Metric (partial) invariance is sufficient, since you only compare regression coefficients and not mean differences (correct?).
4. In your SEM I can't see that the constraints for the measurement model are incorporated.
5. The Wald tests are not wrong. However, I don't understand the meaning perfectly. The approach is at least exploratory. Normally you have hypotheses in advance, don't you? 7. I personally would not appply the bootstrap and use Monte Carlo CI. That is just as effective and more efficient.

HTH

Christian

Hi Giulia,

here are a few remarks from my point of view - others may strongly disagree:

1. You are using WLSMV estimation for the CFA. For the SEM you rely on ML. If your data is continuous or you have enough categories (see https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2Fa0029315), then I would estimate both models with ML.
2. Since the data are probably not normally distributed, I would think about a "robust" estimator (MLM or MLR). It's still a ML estimation, but with correction for se and chi-squared. Consequently, you can do the invariance test with a "robust" variant ("satorra.bentler.2010").
3. Metric (partial) invariance is sufficient, since you only compare regression coefficients and not mean differences (correct?).
4. In your SEM I can't see that the constraints for the measurement model are incorporated.
5. The Wald tests are not wrong. However, I don't understand the meaning perfectly. The approach is at least exploratory. Normally you have hypotheses in advance, don't you? Detached from that, you can do it without the Wald tests and test the moderators with your SEM. For example for ATT->IC you can include the following syntax: mod.ATT.IC := a1 - a.
6 I don't understand the line under ## Fixed Covriances. The covariance between ATT and IC is not fixed, but freely estimated. At the same time ATT is explained by IC. Possibly I am reading the syntax wrong at this point - sorry then.
7. I personally would not appply the bootstrap and use Monte Carlo CI. That is just as effective and more efficient.

HTH

Christian

Il giorno ven 9 giu 2023 alle ore 10:54 Christian Arnold <Christia...@hhl.de> ha scritto:
Hi Giulia,

here are a few remarks from my point of view - others may strongly disagree:

1. You are using WLSMV estimation for the CFA. For the SEM you rely on ML. If your data is continuous or you have enough categories (see https://psycnet.apa.org/doiLanding?doi=10.1037%2Fa0029315), then I would estimate both models with ML.
2. Since the data are probably not normally distributed, I would think about a "robust" estimator (MLM or MLR). It's still a ML estimation, but with correction for se and chi-squared. Consequently, you can do the invariance test with a "robust" variant ("satorra.bentler.2010").
3. Metric (partial) invariance is sufficient, since you only compare regression coefficients and not mean differences (correct?).
4. In your SEM I can't see that the constraints for the measurement model are incorporated.
5. The Wald tests are not wrong. However, I don't understand the meaning perfectly. The approach is at least exploratory. Normally you have hypotheses in advance, don't you? Detached from that, you can do it without the Wald tests and test the moderators with your SEM. For example for ATT->IC you can include the following syntax: mod.ATT.IC := a1 - a.
6 I don't understand the line under ## Fixed Covriances. The covariance between ATT and IC is not fixed, but freely estimated. At the same time ATT is explained by IC. Possibly I am reading the syntax wrong at this point - sorry then.
7. I personally would not appply the bootstrap and use Monte Carlo CI. That is just as effective and more efficient.

HTH

Christian
